name: Treaty of Tordesillas
summary: The Treaty of Tordesillas (June 7, 1494), mediated by Pope Alexander VI, divides the non-European world between Spain and Portugal along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. Land east of the line is Portuguese; land west is Spanish. The treaty, a revision of the papal bull Inter Caetera (1493), was negotiated after Columbus's first voyage revealed Spanish claims in the Atlantic. The line, while it was originally intended to be a north-south split of the Atlantic, accidentally gives Portugal Brazil (which its navigator Cabral reaches in 1500), recognized by Spain in a subsequent treaty.

_quarry.structural_significance: First international agreement dividing the world between colonial powers; establishes the framework of Iberian overseas empire; gives Portugal Brazil through the fortuitous placement of the meridian; the treaty is rejected by France, England, and the Netherlands, who build rival colonial empires
